A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

HSV-1 induces a change in the PIP2/PI ratio, and that this change is dependent on virus protein synthesis, but that the virus protein(s) responsible are expressed in the beta (late) stage of virus synthesis.

the HSV-1-induced changes in phosphoinositide turnover are dependent on the synthesis of virus-specific proteins, and are probably not due to a direct effect of the viral DNA on the cell's phosphoinositide cycle.
the HSV-1-induced changes in phosphoinositide turnover and PIP2/PI (phosphatidyl inositol 4-bisphosphate) ratios are dependent on virus-specific protein synthesis.
The main takeaway from our work is that
HSV-1 induces altered polyphosphoinositol metabolism in BHK cells, which is dependent on virus specific proteins synthesized during the beta stage of virus protein production.

the virus-specific protein(s) involved in the altered phosphoinositides metabolism are synthesized in the beta stage, but that the alpha proteins are also involved, since a ts mutant defective in protein synthesis only in the alpha stage showed a reduced response in the inositides.

the HSV-1-induced alteration of polyphospoinositide metabolism is not due to a virus-induced increase in the activity of phosphoinositide-specific phospholipase C, but is due to a virus-specific alteration of the metabolism of polyphosphatidylnositols.
